cards.title: For o since
cards.summary: Con el presente perfecto, for indica cuánto tiempo dura algo y since indica cuándo empezó.
cards.form: for + período (for two years) · since + momento de inicio (since 2020)
uses: For: un período de tiempo (for three days, for a long time).
Since: el momento en que empezó (since May, since I was a child).
Los dos se usan sobre todo con el presente perfecto: I have lived here for… / since…

pitfalls.why: Para algo que empezó en el pasado y sigue ahora se usa el presente perfecto, no el presente.

pitfalls.wrong: I have worked here since three years.
pitfalls.right: I have worked here for three years.
pitfalls.why: Con un período (three years) se usa for; since va con el momento de inicio.

pitfalls.wrong: She has been sick during two days.
pitfalls.right: She has been sick for two days.
pitfalls.why: Para decir cuánto dura algo se usa for, no during.

cards.title: Say o tell
cards.summary: Las dos significan «decir». Tell casi siempre lleva a quién se lo dices (tell me); say no lo necesita.
cards.form: say + algo (+ to + persona) · tell + persona + algo
uses: Say: repetir palabras o decir algo sin nombrar a la persona (She said hello).
Tell + persona: He told me the truth.
Expresiones fijas con tell: tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke.

pitfalls.wrong: She said me that she was tired.
pitfalls.right: She told me that she was tired.
pitfalls.why: Si la persona va justo después del verbo, se usa tell, no say.

pitfalls.wrong: He told that he was busy.
pitfalls.right: He said that he was busy.
pitfalls.why: Tell necesita a quién (told me, told us). Sin persona, usa say.

pitfalls.wrong: Can you say me the time?
pitfalls.right: Can you tell me the time?
pitfalls.why: «Decirme» algo a mí es tell me.
En inglés se dice tell a lie y tell the truth.

cards.title: Too y enough
cards.summary: Too significa «demasiado» y va antes del adjetivo. Enough significa «suficiente»: va después del adjetivo y antes del sustantivo.
cards.form: too + adjetivo · adjetivo + enough · enough + sustantivo
uses: Too: más de lo necesario (too expensive, too late).
Adjetivo + enough: lo necesario (old enough, warm enough).
Enough + sustantivo: enough money, enough time.
Not … enough: falta algo (not big enough).

pitfalls.why: Con adjetivos, enough va después: hot enough.
Con sustantivos, enough va antes: enough money.

pitfalls.wrong: The movie was too much long.
pitfalls.why: Antes de un adjetivo se usa solo too, sin much.
Para decir que algo impide hacer otra cosa se usa too, no very.

examples.en: This bag is too heavy for me.
examples.es: Esta bolsa es demasiado pesada para mí.

examples.en: He isn't old enough to drive.
examples.es: No tiene edad suficiente para manejar.

cards.title: Much, many y a lot of
cards.summary: Las tres expresan cantidad. Many va con sustantivos contables, much con incontables y a lot of con los dos.
cards.form: many + plural · much + incontable · a lot of + los dos
uses: Many: cosas que se cuentan (many friends, many books).
Much: cosas que no se cuentan (much time, much money), sobre todo en negativas y preguntas.
A lot of: con los dos, sobre todo en oraciones afirmativas (a lot of people, a lot of water).
How many / how much para preguntar cantidades.

pitfalls.why: Money es incontable: se usa much.

pitfalls.right: There are a lot of people here.
pitfalls.why: People es plural: many o a lot of, nunca much.

pitfalls.wrong: How much brothers do you have?
pitfalls.right: How many brothers do you have?
pitfalls.why: Para cosas que se cuentan se pregunta how many.

pitfalls.wrong: I have a lot of works.
pitfalls.right: I have a lot of work.
